name: Third Battle of Panipat

phases.title: The two lines face each other
phases.text: The Maratha lines stood a little north of Kala Amb with Bhau and the royal guard in the centre, the Gardis on the left and Holkar and Sindhia on the right. The Afghan line stood to the south with Najib on its left and the Rohillas on its right centre.

phases.title: The Gardis advance and the Rohillas fall back
phases.text: The Maratha left, under Ibrahim Khan, advanced its infantry against the Rohillas. Point-blank salvos sent the Rohillas reeling back to their lines, and the Gardi musketeers held the field for three hours.

phases.title: Bhau charges the Afghan left centre
phases.text: Bhau led a charge against the forces under Shah Wali. The attack nearly broke the Afghan lines, but Shuja-ud-Daulah did not move from his position and the Maratha mounts were exhausted.

phases.title: Scindia attacks Najib and the Afghan reserve is called up
phases.text: The Marathas under Scindia attacked Najib, who fought a defensive action and kept them at bay. Meanwhile Ahmad Shah called up his 15,000 reserve troops from his camp.

phases.title: The Afghan reserves charge
phases.text: Fresh reserves went to support Shah Wali against Bhau in the centre. Some 7,000 Maratha cavalry and infantry were killed before the hand-to-hand fighting began.

phases.title: The Gardis are encircled
phases.text: The Maratha cavalry guarding the Gardis broke its position and went out against the Rohillas. The Rohilla riflemen fired on it, then encircled the Gardis and outflanked the Maratha centre while Shah Wali pressed the front.

phases.title: Holkar and Scindia leave the field
phases.text: Realising the battle was lost, Holkar's and Scindia's contingents merged, and one broke from the Maratha right and escaped south through an opening in the Durrani lines. Bhau and the royal forces fought on.

note: The Marathas blocked the Afghans' northward path and were themselves blocked from going south, so they are drawn to the north and the Afghans to the south. The Maratha left is then the east and the Afghan left the west. The accounts differ in places: Pasand Khan is placed both on the Afghan left wing and against the Maratha left, and which Rohillas fell back first is not clear, so the Rohillas of the Afghan right centre are shown. The kind of troops of Holkar and Sindhia and the route of the contingent that escaped are not given, and the positions of the cavalry under Vinchurkar and Gaikwad are placed by judgement. The line is drawn short; the accounts give the Maratha line as some 12 km across.
